fields.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
fields.note: The listed prohibitions, the written notice requirement and the notice posting requirement all match the document.

fields.quoted_span: subject to administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages including actual damages or three times the amount of one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief

fields.note: The rule's effective_date is empty. The document gives only the passage date (April 14, 2020) and no effective date.

fields.quoted_span: The City of Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board will be administering complaints regarding the Ordinance.
fields.note: The page describes the ordinance as operative and the Rent Board as administering complaints, but it never states an in-force status outright. The status is inferred.

fields.quoted_span: Owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence
fields.note: The owner-occupied exemption and the other listed exemptions match the document. The coverage of rental housing providers in Berkeley is also supported.

fields.quoted_span: On April 14, 2020, Berkeley City Council passed the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (BMC 13.106).
fields.note: The document cites BMC 13.106, and the ordinance name matches.
